rationale: The per-node transitions pin the ordering that was previously inferred. Nodes 5, 1 and 2 rose from accepted 0 to 37 in convergence rounds 1 and 2 with no StopSign present, then nodes 1, 2 and 5 rose from 37 to 38 in round 3, still with no StopSign present. Only in round 4 did a StopSign appear, and it appeared at accepted 38 without raising the accepted index, while node 3 gained its marker at accepted 37. The accepted index was therefore inflated ahead of the marker, and the StopSign later filled the last counted position at index 37, leaving index 36 empty. This update records that sequence, links it to the end-state hole, and restates the interpretation with the ordering as an observed fact rather than an inference.

knowledge.statement: Across seeded run 13 the per-node transitions read c1:n5:0->37:r0, c2:n1:0->37:r0, c2:n2:0->37:r0, c3:n1:37->38:r0, c3:n2:37->38:r0, c3:n3:0->37:r0, c3:n4:0->37:r0, c3:n5:37->38:r0, c4:n1:38->38:r1, c4:n2:38->38:r1, c4:n3:37->37:r1, c4:n5:38->38:r1. Nodes 1, 2 and 5 therefore reached accepted 38 with no StopSign present, and the StopSign appeared one round later without changing the accepted index. At the end those three nodes count 38 positions with index 36 empty and the StopSign at 37, so the accepted index was inflated ahead of the marker and the marker filled the last counted slot.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; accepted index and StopSign presence are sampled after every action and every convergence round and recorded only when either changes.

investigations.hypothesis: After a lossy reconfiguration the sync path inflates a group's accepted index ahead of its content: nodes 5, 1 and 2 reach accepted 37 and then 38 with no StopSign present, and only in the next round does a StopSign appear at accepted 38 without raising the index. Because the index was already one past the real entries, the marker fills the last counted slot at 37 and leaves index 36 empty. The inflated index then lets the shorter group's leader decide 38 without a matching local entry, and the stalled follower's sequence-expected Decides clamp its decided index instead of reconnecting.

knowledge.assertion: Observed ordering: accepted 0 -> 37 -> 38 with no StopSign, then a StopSign at accepted 38 without an index change, leaving the end state of 38 counted positions with index 36 empty and the marker at 37.
The source behavior behind the inflation: sync_log adds one for a StopSign on a prefix that already covers it, raising accepted_idx without placing an entry.
The resulting end state: nodes 1, 2 and 5 count 38 positions with index 36 absent and the marker at 37, while nodes 3 and 4 hold the marker at 36 and count 37.
Explains the leader side: node 4 decides 38 from the inflated group's reported accepted indices without a matching local entry.

interpretations.rationale: The executed receipts now show the mechanism in order as well as its outcome. Receipt 57c3aacc57fa4bb8a9ad0073499ea3c5 ran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed); both declared comparisons are complete and violated, convergence because decided ended at 38,38,37,38,38 and the invariant because p4_gap is 1. Its transitions field records nodes 5, 1 and 2 reaching accepted 37 in rounds 1 and 2 with no StopSign present, then nodes 1, 2 and 5 reaching accepted 38 in round 3, still with no StopSign present, and only in round 4 a StopSign appearing while the accepted index stayed 38, alongside node 3 gaining its marker at accepted 37. The accepted index was therefore inflated ahead of the marker: sync_log adds one for a StopSign on top of a prefix that already covers it, so the counted length grows without an entry, and when the marker later arrives it fills the last counted slot at index 37 rather than creating a new one. The end state confirms this: nodes 1, 2 and 5 report accepted 38 and decided 38 with index 36 empty and the StopSign at 37, while nodes 3 and 4 hold 36 entries followed by the StopSign at 36 and report accepted 37. Node 4, the final leader, merged a StopSign-bearing promise at round 3 and accepted a log ending with the StopSign at 36, yet reports decided 38 because handle_accepted takes the inflated group's reported accepted index once is_chosen counts a quorum, without comparing it to its own accepted index or requiring a matching local entry. Node 3, decided 37 with accepted 37, receives the Decides with sequence counters 2 and 3 as its next expected messages, so handle_decide clamps decided to 37; it sends no PrepareReq, is offered no AcceptStopSign because it already accepted one, and repeated Decides reuse a consumed sequence number, so it remains behind for the whole window. The zero divergence figure in earlier receipts is an artifact of the comparison helper, which keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix and therefore cannot see a hole, a marker at a different index or a prefix-length difference.
counterevidence: A follower that genuinely missed the AcceptStopSign can still recover: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead, the follower reconnected, and an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, which gives the follower a fresh sequence and a log sync from the new leader.
The earlier zero divergence count is not counterevidence of agreement; it is an artifact of a comparison that ignores StopSign entries, holes and prefix lengths.
limitations: Transitions are sampled after each action and each convergence round, so a change and its reversal between samples would be missed; none is evident here.
The exact log_sync payloads that inflated the accepted indices were not recorded; the link to sync_log's StopSign arithmetic rests on the observed ordering and the source.
Node 3's inbound trace is capped at twelve messages after the lossy phase, and Promises to node 4 are recorded only when delivered and only up to forty entries.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
